title: Status and Perspectives of Lifetime Measurements on Ions of Iron Group Elements
content: Multiply charged ions of iron dominate the EUV spectrum of the solar corona, but ions of other iron group elements are also present. A number of electric dipole and higher-multipole order transition rates in such ions have been measured over the years, mostly by beam-foil spectroscopy, in heavy-ion storage rings, and in various ion traps. The experiments relate mostly to three ranges of atomic lifetimes, i.e., picosecond lifetimes of 3p levels with spin-conserving E1 decays, multi-nanosecond lifetimes of levels with spin-changing (intercombination) E1 decays, and millisecond to multi-second lifetimes of 3p and 3d levels without any E1 decay channel. The state of the knowledge base is assessed, and the problems of further progress are outlined.
